content: Happy to answer any questions here for #Event announcements > Caltech Mathathon Challenge @ 💬

A figure of $2M in compute tokens is mentioned. How is that distributed? ($2m for the entire competition? $2M per team? $2M per project decided by the assembly of teams?)

Is it enough that one representative of a team be physically present, with communication allowed to remote team members?

Will any virtual mode be possible, including a spectator-only presence?
sender_full_name: J. J. Issai (project started by GRP)

content: Who will be on the judging panel for sure? I think it would be more appealing for people to apply if there were some well-known mathematicians among the judges.

J. J. Issai (project started by GRP) said:

A figure of $2M in compute tokens is mentioned. How is that distributed? ($2m for the entire competition? $2M per team? $2M per project decided by the assembly of teams?)

Is it enough that one representative of a team be physically present, with communication allowed to remote team members?

Will any virtual mode be possible, including a spectator-only presence?

  1. $20k per team for $2M in total!
  2. No, we require all participants to physically attend the event. We cover all travel expenses. This is because we want human collaborations and connections to result from this event, not just human talking to the AI:)
  3. Judging can be online. Also just to clarify there are almost 2 stages of verification, one will happen in person and the second stage will happen several months after cause we want people to validate all the solutions and approve them from experts and eventually make it into a publication if needed!

Yongxi Lin (Aaron) said:

Who will be on the judging panel for sure? I think it would be more appealing for people to apply if there were some well-known mathematicians among the judges.

we have a dozen judges so far, like Elliot Glazer, Kaiyu Yang, Lingfu Zhang, Tony yu etc and are trying to contact more profs: )! Sergei Gukov is also a speaker for the event! We do want diverse mathematicians to apply to be judges, the more the better across various domains
This sounds very cool! Just to make sure, who broadly is in the target group for participants (career-stage wise)?
Is this oriented towards academics, people working in AI labs, anyone with a mathematics result made with AI, or anyone whatsoever? How is acceptance even defined? Is this also, only for US citizens?

What happens if a team does not solve their open conjecture, or build a new theory? Or does "results" just mean "whatever you learned during the mathathon"?

This thread on X says "sponsors provide their own tracks consisting of pre-written problems". Is there a place to see those problems?
https://x.com/_sathvikr/status/2095991589742985602

Sebastián Rodrigo said:

Is this oriented towards academics, people working in AI labs, anyone with a mathematics result made with AI, or anyone whatsoever? How is acceptance even defined? Is this also, only for US citizens?

  1. It’s oriented toward academics. Right now, most of our applicants are math grad students and professors.
  2. We will also admit undergrads who have demonstrated their mathematical aptitude. E.g. IMO gold medalists. One of our goals is to identify how AI changes the balance between talent and experience, so it’s important to admit a diverse set of participants.
  3. We admit people based on their perceived mathematical talent.
  4. We welcome international applicants and fully cover their travel. But they must obtain a visa to visit the US.
By when can we expect to hear back?
I'm sure many of you are aware of this by now, but let me mention https://proofsandprompts.com/2026/09/10/open-letter-about-the-mathathon/, which I invite you to read and support.
